problem: Standard ROS navigation planners either re-plan or freeze when people block the robot's path; they do not treat the human as an interactive agent that can be asked to make way.
motivation: Social robots in public spaces need polite, human-like behaviour, and the natural human response to a blocked path is to ask for permission to pass. Prior work on this (e.g. Vega et al. 2018) was only shown in simulation, so a deployed, functional implementation is missing.
key_idea: Add a high-level situation assessment layer that detects when the local planner fails because of a person, compares the alternative path against the original, and if no good detour exists, stops and verbally asks the person to let the robot pass.
insight: Existing open-source navigation and lightweight CPU person detection can be combined to bring HRI into the navigation loop, and a 'level of consideration' threshold on path-length difference lets the robot decide between detouring and interacting. Evidence is qualitative only (three hallway scenarios, preliminary trials); there are no ablations.
method: Navigation: ROS navigation stack (amcl, dwa_local_planner, gmapping), with depth image converted to virtual laser scans via depthimage_to_laserscan because of Pepper's short laser range.

People Perception: OpenCV dnn MobileNet-SSD (Caffe) for person detection, then a Dlib correlation tracker; a message is published only when the bounding box is wider than 80 px, to filter far-away people.
Failure trigger: the time the local planner cannot find a valid plan is exposed to trigger the situation assessment before the standard recovery behaviors.
Obstacle clustering: on local plan failure, virtual laser data is clustered with MeanShift (quantile 0.20); if a cluster mean is under 3 m, people perception runs for t seconds.
Path comparison / level of consideration: a new global path is compared to the original by length; if it is shorter or equal within a threshold, the robot takes it and avoids interaction.
Interaction: otherwise navigation is stopped and the robot asks permission verbally; if still blocked it waits 5 s and asks again, or can freeze.
Orchestration: a NAOqi Navigation App loads destinations from JSON into a Location server and talks to ROS via ActionLib.

setting.backbone: MobileNet-SSD (Caffe, pretrained, frozen) + ROS navigation stack (amcl, DWA)
setting.training_data: none (uses a pretrained MobileNet-SSD; no training done)
setting.observation: Pepper depth camera (converted to virtual laser) + RGB image for person detection + onboard lasers
setting.action_space: ROS navigation velocity commands (omnidirectional wheeled base) plus verbal request
setting.privileged: prior map from gmapping plus a sketched map of the scenario

numbers_note: No quantitative results; only qualitative hallway scenarios shown in figures.
results: Qualitatively, in a hallway the robot takes the shortest path when free and a longer detour when blocked. When people block it, it asks for permission and then proceeds on a plan no longer than the original. In one trial an unexpected human-human collaboration occurred, where one person asked the other to move.
limitations: Computation is off-board on an external CPU, and network segmentation degrades the people perception module.
The situation assessment is not embedded in the ROS local planner.
Only preliminary qualitative trials with no quantitative evaluation; the social modulation of the level of consideration is future work.
compares_to: ROS navigation stack baseline (re-plan or freeze)
